samples.question: The board is scattered with decorative coloured tiles, and exactly one cream panel sits somewhere on it. Only what is drawn on the cream panel decides the answer; every tile off the panel is decoration and means nothing. The panel carries three separate shapes, each built from small square tiles laid on a regular grid with cream showing between the tiles. The upper shape is the gray SOCKET: a 5-by-5 block of tiles with a hole bitten out of it. The hole is a connected group of 3, 4 or 5 missing tiles and it never touches the socket's outer border, so the socket's 5-by-5 outline is always complete. Below the socket are two PLUGS, one on the left and one on the right. Each plug is a single colour, the two plugs have different colours, and both colours come from red, blue, green and purple. Each plug is built from exactly as many tiles as the hole is missing, and both plugs have the same overall width and height in tiles. Exactly one of the two plugs would fill the hole exactly if it were slid straight into it, with no turning and no mirror-flipping; the other plug is the same tiles in a different arrangement and would not fit. What colour is the plug that fits the hole? Answer red, blue, green or purple.
